name: TranslatorService mode `gloss`: a morphology-aware word-by-word Romanian to English gloss as the input of LanguageProofingLLM (measurement of the gloss itself, no training)
frozen_before_results: NOT frozen before the first measurements: the gloss was developed iteratively on the dev2300 sample and its read sub-samples (seeds 3, 5, 11, 21, 22) and the dev held-out words, so those numbers are development numbers. This record was written after the code was frozen (lib/translator-service/backends/gloss.mjs sha256 ab6ffb49a2f779d880e4cae7bdeeeedf7b71aa3ee388c2e3a0d8b41ae9270187, symbolic.mjs b8fd5bd6...) and before the final runs reported in the summary; the final runs used only the frozen code. The two read samples reported as accuracy (seed 99, 50 Romanian sentences; seed 98, 30 mixed sentences, both from the full dev split) and the niche probe of eval-translator-compare-v1 were read after the freeze. The romglish probe (30 sentences) was written by the author of the rules and is a demonstration, not an independent test.
owner_request: Owner idea 2026-10-01 (translated): use the dictionaries intelligently; recognise the grammatical forms, do a word-by-word translation Romanian-English in the grammatically correct forms; would that be enough for LanguageProofingLLM to rephrase it into decent, useful English? Follow-up of the same day: the gloss must also work on romgleza.
questions: Q1: how much of the Romanian content vocabulary does the gloss translate (coverage) and how often is the chosen English word right (read samples)?

Q2: do the words held out from iteration 2 (and the eight words held out from iteration 3) appear in the gloss, and does feeding the gloss to the existing iteration-2 model (no retraining) raise vocabulary accuracy?
Q3: how often does the gloss alone pass the clean-English gate and the analysis gate?
Q4: does the gloss handle mixed text (English frame, Romanian frame, English stems with Romanian enclitics, Romanian-inflected English verbs)?
Q5: end-to-end chain latency and agreement with the message-only chain.

hypotheses.H1: Held-out words: the target word is present in the gloss alone in more outputs than in the unrewritten message, with a paired bootstrap 95% interval above 0 (ten words, 574 pairs; eight words, 830 pairs).
hypotheses.H2: The untrained iteration-2 model keeps the glossed words (it raises its own rate on the ten held-out words), but it is not a post-editor of the gloss: on the chain proxy the gloss chain is not better than the message-only chain.
hypotheses.H3: The gloss alone passes the clean-English gate in at least 95% of the repair units of the dev sample.
hypotheses.non_claim: Not a claim about translation quality in general: coverage is that of the host dictionary on the vocabulary of this synthetic corpus (whose generator vocabulary is part of the dictionary); out-of-domain accuracy is the niche probe.
